reports.text:

reports.title: Lake Success Report
reports.text: Success Lake remained near 10% of its storage capacity, and plenty of good-sized largemouth bass took jigs, hula grubs, and drop-shot finesse baits in baitfish, green pumpkin, and purple patterns. Bass held near the trees, steep rocky banks, and along the dam in 10 to 20 feet of water. Crappie anglers focused on submerged vegetation, using slip bobbers and small live minnows at depths of around 15 feet.

reports.text:
I’ve spent a lot of time fishing bait finesse system (BFS) gear over the past several years, and one of the things I’ve learned is that a good BFS reel needs to do more than simply cast lightweight lures. reports.text:
You can find countless hook brands and styles on the market now. But, in my opinion, none are as versatile as the Gamakatsu EWG (Extra Wide Gap). This hook has dozens of applications in the bass fishing space, from rigging soft plastics to its incorporation into swing heads and even some skirted baits.

Crappie Basics: Match the Hatch for More Crappie

One of the simplest ways to improve your crappie fishing is to give the fish what they’re already looking for. That means matching your jig to the size and general shape of the forage crappie are feeding on.
If 2-inch minnows make up a big part of the crappie diet in the lake you’re fishing, for example, a 2-inch jig is a logical choice. reports.title: Yeopim Creek Fliers with Carolina ALL OUT
reports.text:
Fliers are among the most unique panfish in the Carolinas
T he Carolinas are full of numerous species of panfish, and for their size, they all fight like champs. They’re also very tasty. Fliers, although they are found throughout the southeast, are among the least widely distributed panfish, mostly living in swampy, acidic blackwater creeks with low pH.
Where you’ll find fliers, you can always count on finding other panfish as well. They overlap with crappie, bluegill, redbreast and shellcrackers, among other species.

reports.title: How To: Hot Summertime Tactics for catching crappie
reports.text:
Hot Summertime Tactics for Catching Crappie
When summer water gets hot, crappie usually leave the shallow cover and seek cooler, more oxygenated water, shade, and baitfish. The key is finding where those conditions overlap.
Fish deeper: Start around 15–30 feet, then adjust based on your lake’s depth and thermocline. Electronics are extremely helpful for locating suspended schools.
Target brush piles: Deep brush, submerged trees, and man-made structure can hold crappie throughout summer. Slowly work a jig vertically around the cover.
Follow the bait: Find schools of shad or other forage and look nearby—and often directly beneath them—for crappie.
